page: Microsoft Azure DC4as_v6 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Built on an AMD processor architecture, the instance provides four dedicated virtual processing units paired with 16.0 GB of system memory. This configuration implements an industry-standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio, yielding exactly 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance architecture does not incorporate dedicated graphics processors, maintaining a zero GPU profile.

The instance contains no integrated local storage volumes. Storage functionality is handled exclusively through remote network-attached disks via Azure Premium Storage capabilities, ensuring that operational data persistence and throughput depend on selected external volumes. In terms of direct network provisioning, the virtual machine includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating configured virtual network interfaces or separate IP resources for external access.

By omitting integrated local scratch drives and specialized accelerator silicon, the DC4as_v6 maintains cost efficiency for infrastructure tiers that do not require high-speed ephemeral disks. Dedicated core assignment ensures predictable processing capacity for uninterrupted compute cycles. Primary workload fits include multi-tier web applications, REST API gateways, container orchestration nodes, integration testing pipelines, and intermediate microservices backed by external storage.
description: Microsoft Azure DC4as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance within the DCasv6 series, operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The hardware profile features four dedicated x86_64 vCPUs powered by an AMD processor, accompanied by 16.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes no onboard graphical processing units and provisions no local disk storage, requiring external volume attachments through its Premium Storage capability for persistent state and file system operations. It also includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses by default. Operating with dedicated vCPU allocation and a balanced memory-to-core proportion, the configuration offers resource efficiency for general business logic without the overhead of unneeded accelerator hardware. Microsoft Azure DC4as_v6 is positioned for intermediate general-purpose workloads, including web application serving, backend API hosting, containerized microservices, and light database applications relying on attached network storage.
